title: Understanding the Heat Index and Why It's Soaring
seoTitle: What is the Heat Index and Why is it Rising?
subtitle: Intense heat and humidity are pushing felt temperatures above 100 degrees
excerpt: Heatwaves and high humidity are pushing the heat index above 100 degrees in some regions, prompting alerts and prevention recommendations for the public.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Temperatures near 90 degrees combined with high humidity are causing the heat index to exceed the 100-degree mark in several areas, prompting the issuance of weather alerts this Wednesday and Thursday.

What the Heat Index Means

The heat index represents the perceived temperature the human body experiences when air temperature combines with relative humidity. When humidity is high, sweat evaporation decreases, making the sensation of heat feel greater than the measured temperature.

How the Heat Index is Being Measured This Week

In Central Virginia regions, heat index values range between 100 and 105 degrees, while in the Shenandoah Valley, they reach 100 degrees or slightly higher. In other areas, the combination of 90 to 95-degree temperatures with high humidity causes the heat index to exceed 100 degrees in some spots.

Health Impacts

High heat index values increase the risk of dehydration, exhaustion, and heatstroke. Therefore, alerts recommend constant hydration, frequent breaks when working outdoors, and special attention to the elderly and pets.

Recommendations for Facing the Heat

Guidelines include staying in air-conditioned environments, limiting sun exposure during the hottest parts of the day, wearing light clothing, and drinking plenty of water. It is also advised to check on neighbors, especially the most vulnerable.

Forecast for the Coming Days

The intense heat is expected to last until the end of the week, with a possibility of light evening showers. A slow-moving cold front is anticipated to arrive on Saturday, bringing temperatures back into the 80s and reducing the perceived heat. The Labor Day weekend should feature cooler and less humid conditions.

With information from WSET, WVIR.
